doc.title: George Benson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: PBS special recreating the Benny Goodman sextet
summary: Creed Taylor and Hammond get Benson on a PBS Goodman tribute with Red Norvo, Jo Jones and Teddy Wilson; he can't recall all the personnel.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: If we could go and talk about your experience on that PBS series, Soundstage, where you came on and did a re-creation of the Benny Goodman sextet with . . .

Man, that was an incredible – Creed Taylor had been trying to convince Benny Goodman that I was the second Charlie Christian. I mean, I don’t believe that, but he thought that I was a close second to Charlie. So he invited me out to the PBS special they had honoring Benny Goodman, and they tried to put together a band that was similar, or some of the guys from his alumni – alumni from his other band. I think we had Red Norvo. Norvo was playing the vibes, and my favorite, Jo Jones, playing drums.
Um-hmm. And what’s the great piano player, his name? And was it Mule on bass? No. The band – the guys who used to play in his – oh, Edwards? Was it Teddy Edwards? No. I can’t recall.
I’ve got a recording that you did for Columbia that had Benny Goodman on clarinet, Al Grey, trombone, John Bunch, piano.
No, no. That’s the recording. That wasn’t even a great one.
Let’s just see if there are any . . .
No. On the PBS special, we had his – Wilson, I think was . . .
I think that’s him, Teddy Wilson.
Oh yeah. He was in the original trio with Gates – [Lionel] Hampton – and Gene Krupa. So that’s Teddy Wilson, right.
